newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline softer with NYMEX but supported.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline softer with NYMEX but supported.

text.p: NWE gasoline was a touch softer with NYMEX gasoline weakening in afternoon trade but interest to take product transatlantic remained supportive, despite expensive freight costs, traders said.
They said light inland demand ahead of the holiday season was also supportive although this was being satisfied by local supplies without recourse to the ARA market.
Eurograde barges traded at $225.50 and $225 a tonne fob ARA in early business. Both buyers were U.S. trade houses who are thought to be looking to build cargoes for arbitrage.
High freight costs continue to restrict arbitrage trade but traders said that some players may have time chartered vessels at preferential rates that make it workable.
Eurograde cargoes valued around $225 a tonne cif NWE with fob liftings discounted by around $10 a tonne.
Trader buying interest was also seen in the Mediterranean for product to go into Africa.
